report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of daedalus/eval/ceiling.py; all docstring claims in this window are kept; no broken or uncheckable claims found.

handoff.purpose: Compute temporal co-change ceiling metrics (clean/leaky arms), render report, and provide CLI entry point.

symbols.name: _def_count
symbols.note: Closure returning count_of; sums counts over alias-expanded symbols for a given arm revision.

symbols.name: count_of
symbols.note: Inner function in _def_count; sums counts for sorted aliases of a symbol.

symbols.name: _summary
symbols.note: Aggregates class counts across per_task for a given key (classes_clean/classes_leaky).

symbols.name: _ceiling
symbols.note: Returns REACHABLE count divided by denominator, or 0.0 if denominator is zero.

symbols.name: render_ceiling
symbols.note: Builds ASCII-only report string from result dict; includes static-edge and reachable audits, merge/backtest notes, alias probe failures, and reopen signal.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entry point; parses --min-count, calls temporal_ceiling, renders, prints with ASCII fallback.

claims.why: All string literals in render_ceiling are ASCII; the only non-ASCII path is in main's fallback which encodes to ASCII with replacement.

claims.text: This is a walk-forward BACKTEST HIT-RATE (best case for temporal coupling), NOT slicer recall -- see daedalus/eval/ceiling.py.
claims.why: The rendered header explicitly states this is a backtest hit-rate upper bound, not slicer recall; the computation uses REACHABLE over missed labels.

claims.text: the gap between the two arms is the self-prediction artifact: coupling that exists only because the minted commit is counted
claims.why: The leaky arm includes full history (including mint commit) while clean arm excludes it; the displayed gap is the difference in ceilings, which is the stated artifact.

claims.text: a missed label's defining file is ALREADY a static neighbour of the focus. That is edge-but-dropped -- a slicer defect, strictly more important than anything temporal. Fix that first
claims.why: The code lists STATIC_EDGE misses and instructs to fix them first; the message accurately describes the situation.

claims.text: clean-arm REACHABLE labels (audit these -- each is a claim that pre-mint history named the file)
claims.why: The code lists REACHABLE labels from classes_clean, which are those where pre-mint history (clean arm) named the file.

claims.text: minted at a MERGE commit; clean arm is first-parent history only.
claims.why: The code appends a note when merge_commit is true; the note text matches the claim.

claims.text: has no backtest rev (...) clean arm not scored.
claims.why: The code appends a note when backtest_rev_reason is truthy; the note text matches.

claims.text: those files were scored rename-BLIND and the ceiling may be understated.
claims.why: The code appends a warning when alias_probe_failures is non-zero, exactly as described.

claims.text: REOPEN signal: clean rename-aware ceiling clears the materiality floor (...) -- the temporal-enrichment lane may be worth reopening (see module docstring).
claims.why: The code checks reopen_temporal_lane and prints the signal with the floor description.

claims.text: ...measured at min_count=1, BELOW the reopen threshold: a single co-occurrence is one data point, not a pattern (churn.py). The reopen condition is defined at min_count >= 2.
claims.why: The code appends this note when min_count < 2, matching the claim.

claims.text: reopen signal: none -- {n_reach} clean-reachable label(s) in {n_tasks_reachable_clean} task(s) is below the materiality floor (...)
claims.why: The code prints this message when n_reach is non-zero but reopen_temporal_lane is false.

claims.text: reopen signal: none -- clean ceiling is zero; the temporal lane stays closed.
claims.why: The code prints this message when both reopen_temporal_lane and n_reach are false.
main only calls temporal_ceiling and prints; no writes or side effects.

observations.what: The clean arm is not scored when backtest_rev is None; classes_clean is set to NO_BACKTEST_REV for all missed labels. This is reflected in n_scored_clean which subtracts NO_BACKTEST_REV from n_labels.

The reopen signal uses OR of share and tasks, but the floor text says 'share OR tasks' which matches. The min_count<2 note says the reopen condition is defined at min_count >=2, but the code does not enforce that; it only adds a note.
The render uses result['summary_clean'].get('REACHABLE', 0) for n_reach, which counts labels not tasks; the message says 'label(s) in N task(s)' which is accurate.
